home-remodeling.title: Gut Renovations, Sea Ranch Lakes FL | PGX Builders
home-remodeling.meta_description: We gut 1950s Sea Ranch Lakes village houses to the block and rebuild them permitted, inspected and approved by the Village. (786) 273-2524.
home-remodeling.hero_sub: Whole-home remodels for the 1950s and 1960s houses of Sea Ranch Lakes: structure, mechanicals, impact glass and finishes, permitted through the Village, supervised daily, built by a licensed Florida general contractor, Lic. CGC1539072.
home-remodeling.local_heading: A village of two hundred houses
intro_paragraphs: Sea Ranch Lakes was developed in the mid-1950s and incorporated as a village in October 1959, and the original inventory still shows it: low block houses with terrazzo floors, jalousie windows and eight-foot ceilings, sitting on lanes named after lakes. Fewer than two hundred homes fill the gate. Some front the Intracoastal, some sit on Lake Cayuga and Lake Seneca, and the rest line interior lanes such as Minnetonka, Saranac and Chippewa. Owners here rarely tear one down. They gut it, replace everything behind the walls, and finally give the floor plan a reason to face the water.

Permitting in a village this size does not work the way it does in a city. Applications go to the Village Clerk at the Gatehouse Road office, the Village's building official and consulting professionals review them against the Florida Building Code and the Village land development code, a citizen advisory board drawn from Beach Club members comments on design and aesthetics, and the Village Council takes the final action. Broward sits inside the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so impact openings need HVHZ product approval, under code administration set countywide by the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals.

Twenty-plus years in South Florida and more than 150 remodels and additions, every one permitted and inspected, is what we bring to a street where everyone knows whose truck is parked where. Scope is fixed in writing before demolition, and a supervisor is here every working day. Deliveries clear the guard at the single entrance, the private lanes stay clean, and the trades keep village hours. One team runs the job from estimate through final inspection and warranty, so when a neighbor on the advisory board asks how it is going, you have an answer.
home-remodeling.scope_heading: What we replace, what we keep
home-remodeling.scope_intro: Nothing begins until the scope is written down and priced. These are the pieces that recur in a Sea Ranch Lakes gut renovation.

scope_items.name: Opening the block plan
scope_items.desc: Removing interior block partitions from a 1950s layout, with engineered beams and columns sized, sealed and permitted before the first wall comes down.

scope_items.name: Pipes, panels and ducts
scope_items.desc: New service and panel, replacement of original galvanized supply and cast iron waste, and ducted high-efficiency cooling sized for a house with real glass.

scope_items.name: Impact glass, HVHZ approved
scope_items.desc: Windows, sliders and doors carrying High-Velocity Hurricane Zone approval, installed with the buck, anchor and sealant details this coastal exposure genuinely demands.

scope_items.name: Roof and envelope
scope_items.desc: Re-roof coordination, tie-beam and connection upgrades where a 1960s structure needs them, and wall assemblies detailed to keep salt air on the outside.

scope_items.name: Raised ceilings and finish work
scope_items.desc: Flat ceilings lifted where the structure allows it, terrazzo restored or replaced, and millwork built to the proportions the new rooms ask for.

faqs.q: Does the Village Council really sign off on my plans?
faqs.a: For work that needs development approval, yes. Applications land with the Village Clerk, whose role in actually issuing the permit is ministerial. The Village's building official reviews against the building and land development codes, a citizen advisory board of Beach Club members weighs in on design and aesthetics, and the Council takes the final action. The approval that counts is the Council's, so keep every comment and condition in writing rather than relying on a hallway conversation.

faqs.q: Is it realistic to stay in the house during a full gut?
faqs.a: Almost never for the heavy phase, and we say so at the walk-through rather than three weeks in. With ceilings open, no cooling and no kitchen, a slab house of this vintage is not somewhere to camp. Many owners here are seasonal and simply time the work for the months they are north. If you must stay, we phase it, seal it and keep one wing conditioned, and it still costs schedule.

faqs.q: What is different about building inside a gated village this small?
faqs.a: Logistics, mostly. There is one guarded entrance, and the Village itself owns no land inside its own borders: the streets, the lakes and the beach club property belong to the Sea Ranch Beach Club. So staging, dumpster placement and access all get negotiated rather than assumed. Fire and rescue arrive from Pompano Beach. Crews check in, park where they are told, and leave the lane clean. None of that is difficult. All of it has to be planned before day one.

faqs.q: What is a realistic timeline from first meeting to finished house?
faqs.a: Design, engineering and Village approval usually occupy several months before anyone swings a hammer, because the Council meets on its own calendar and the advisory board comments before it. Construction on a full interior gut with new mechanicals and impact glass commonly runs from six months to a year, longer when the roof and structure are in scope. You get a written schedule with the estimate and daily supervision defending it, plus a realistic read on which dates depend on the Village rather than on us.

faqs.q: Why is a high-end number so far above the low bid?
faqs.a: Because the low bid is usually missing the parts nobody can see. In a house from this era the real budget lives in re-piping, electrical service, roof and envelope, HVHZ openings and structural work, none of which photograph well. We scope those in writing with real allowances before you sign, so the figure you approve is the figure you pay unless something genuinely unforeseen appears and we document it. PGX competes on that, not on price.

home-remodeling.cta_sub: Bring the survey and the wish list. We walk the village house, price it honestly, and write it all down, in English o en español.

kitchen-remodeling.title: Sea Ranch Lakes Kitchen Remodeling, FL | PGX Builders
kitchen-remodeling.meta_description: Custom kitchen remodeling in Sea Ranch Lakes, FL — cabinetry, stone, and the wall between your galley and Lake Cayuga. Book a walk-through: (786) 273-2524.
kitchen-remodeling.h1: A kitchen that faces the lake
kitchen-remodeling.hero_sub: Custom cabinetry, stone counters and structural openings for Sea Ranch Lakes kitchens, including the block wall standing between you and the water, permitted through the Village office and supervised daily by a licensed general contractor.
kitchen-remodeling.local_heading: Where the 1958 galley used to be
intro_paragraphs: Houses on Cayuga Road and Seneca Road were built when a kitchen was a galley with a pass-through, tucked at the back beside the carport and walled off from the Florida room. The lake is on the far side of that wall. So a kitchen project in Sea Ranch Lakes is usually the same story in different finishes: take out the partition, absorb the old utility room or breakfast nook, set an island where the pass-through was, and let whoever is cooking look at the water like everybody else in the house.

Kitchen work touching plumbing, electrical, mechanical or structure gets permitted through the Village office on Gatehouse Road, where the Village's building official reviews plans against the Florida Building Code as administered in Broward County. If the scope stays inside the walls, the path is short. Enlarge the window over the sink or cut a new opening to the terrace and you are changing the exterior, which brings design comment from the Beach Club citizen board and action by the Village Council. Older houses here also tend to need an electrical service upgrade before a modern appliance package is legal.

Structure and rough-ins go first, then boxes set and leveled, then stone templated off the actual cabinets rather than off a drawing. Selections are locked before demolition so nothing sits waiting on a backordered hood. Adjacent rooms get papered, taped and protected, because in a house this size the dust has nowhere else to go. Fixed written scope, one supervisor on site daily, one accountable team from estimate to warranty. Licensed and insured under Lic. CGC1539072, with 20-plus years of South Florida work behind it.
kitchen-remodeling.scope_heading: The new kitchen, piece by piece
kitchen-remodeling.scope_intro: Every line is priced before a single cabinet is ordered. These are the elements that appear in nearly every village kitchen we build.

scope_items.name: Cabinetry built to fit
scope_items.desc: Made-to-order boxes and doors scaled to eight-foot ceilings, finished for coastal humidity, with interiors specified around how you actually store things.

scope_items.name: The wall to the lake
scope_items.desc: Load path calculated, beam engineered and permitted, then the block partition between the old galley and the water view comes out for good.

scope_items.name: Islands templated in place
scope_items.desc: Marble, quartzite or porcelain templated in place, with island framing engineered for the weight and any seating overhang carried on real steel.

scope_items.name: Appliances relocated and vented
scope_items.desc: Relocated ranges, hoods, refrigeration and wine storage on dedicated circuits, with permitted gas runs and exterior venting detailed so nothing whistles in a squall.

scope_items.name: Power the house lacks
scope_items.desc: Panel and service upgrades coordinated with the underground feeds, plus layered lighting on separate controls instead of one glaring fixture in the ceiling.

faqs.q: Does a kitchen remodel here have to go past the Village Clerk?
faqs.a: If it touches plumbing, electrical, mechanical or structure, and a real kitchen touches all four, then yes. The application moves through the Village office and gets inspected as work proceeds. Cosmetic swaps into existing hookups do not. Unpermitted work has a habit of surfacing in a village where two hundred owners talk to each other and every resale gets read closely, and retroactive permitting is the expensive route.

faqs.q: Can the wall between the kitchen and the Florida room come out?
faqs.a: Usually. These are concrete block houses with cast tie beams, so an interior partition often carries less than owners fear, but only an engineer can answer it honestly. We open a small inspection area, get the load path calculated and sealed, then permit the beam. Occasionally the wall is doing real work and the answer is a beam and column pair rather than a clean opening. Either way, you see the drawing before you see a price.

faqs.q: Will a proper island even fit in a house this size?
faqs.a: More often than the original floor plan suggests, because the square footage already exists. It is simply divided into a galley, a utility room and a breakfast nook nobody uses. Combining those usually yields a room that takes a real island with seating. What we will not do is force one in that leaves you sidling past an open dishwasher. Where the space truly resists, a peninsula and a smarter layout beat a bad island.

faqs.q: How long does the kitchen stay out of service?
faqs.a: Custom cabinetry drives the calendar. Quality packages take months to fabricate, so we order early and hold demolition until the shop confirms delivery. On-site work generally runs a couple of months, longer when a structural opening or a service upgrade is involved. Seasonal owners often schedule the whole thing for summer and return in November to a finished room. We set up a temporary kitchen either way.

faqs.q: What actually drives the price of a kitchen at this level?
faqs.a: Cabinetry and stone lead, appliances follow closely, then come the invisible items: the structural opening, the panel upgrade, the plumbing you are relocating. Two quotes for the same kitchen usually differ because one of them assumed the electrical was fine. We walk it, scope it, and set a fixed number against a written specification. Certainty is what we sell, rather than being the lowest of three numbers.

kitchen-remodeling.cta_sub: Show us the room and the view it is currently hiding. We send back a fixed written scope, in English o en español.

bathroom-remodeling.title: Bathroom Renovations in Sea Ranch Lakes, FL | PGX Builders
bathroom-remodeling.meta_description: Sea Ranch Lakes bath remodels carve a real suite out of a 1960s plan, with Village permits and flood-tested pans. PGX, (786) 273-2524.
bathroom-remodeling.h1: The primary suite the ranch never had
bathroom-remodeling.hero_sub: Primary suites, guest baths and powder rooms across Sea Ranch Lakes: frameless glass, stone, flood-tested pans and honest plumbing replacement, permitted through the Village and supervised daily by a licensed, insured general contractor.
bathroom-remodeling.local_heading: Small baths, big houses, old pipes
intro_paragraphs: The houses on Winnebago Road, Oneida Lane and Tahoe Lane were designed around a hall bath and a modest primary with a five-foot tub, because that is what a 1960 beach house needed. Nobody was picturing a double vanity, a freestanding tub and a shower with two heads. So a bathroom project in Sea Ranch Lakes is usually a land grab: a small fourth bedroom or an oversized closet gets folded into the primary, the hall bath gets rebuilt properly for guests, and the powder room stops being an afterthought off the carport.

Bath permits are pulled through the Village office and inspected in sequence, which is exactly what you want when waterproofing and rough plumbing are about to vanish behind stone. Two local realities shape the scope. These are slab-on-grade houses, so relocating a drain means cutting and re-pouring concrete, and the original cast iron and galvanized lines have reached the end of their service life. And adding or enlarging an exterior window alters the elevation, which sends the design to the Beach Club citizen board and the Village Council before the permit moves forward.

A bathroom is the least forgiving room in a house. Membranes get flood-tested and documented before tile is set, pans get sloped to a level rather than to a feeling, and heavy glass hangs on blocking we installed on purpose. Stone is templated and handled by people who have earned the right to touch it. You get a written scope, a daily supervisor, protected paths through the rest of the house, and permits and inspections on everything. Lic. CGC1539072, licensed and insured, with more than 150 remodels and additions behind us.
bathroom-remodeling.scope_heading: How a Village bath gets rebuilt
bathroom-remodeling.scope_intro: From a powder room to a full primary suite, the scope is settled on paper before a single tile gets ordered.

scope_items.name: Borrowing the fourth bedroom
scope_items.desc: Reworking bedroom, closet and hall bath square footage into one suite, with layout, structure and rough-ins permitted as a single coordinated package.

scope_items.name: Slab work done once
scope_items.desc: Cutting, rerouting and re-pouring the slab where drains have to move, then pressure-testing before anything closes, because concrete is unforgiving of second attempts.

scope_items.name: Pans flooded, then tiled
scope_items.desc: Curbless entries where the slab allows, sloped pans, linear drains, and waterproofing that gets filled with water and watched before tile arrives.

scope_items.name: New supply and drains
scope_items.desc: Replacing original galvanized supply and cast iron waste while the walls are open, which is the only moment it will ever be inexpensive.

scope_items.name: Air, heat and lighting
scope_items.desc: Exhaust terminated through the roof, a heated floor for the cool mornings, and mirror lighting from the sides rather than one can in the ceiling.

faqs.q: Do bathroom remodels need permits in Sea Ranch Lakes?
faqs.a: Anything past paint and a new mirror does. Moving plumbing, altering circuits and changing ventilation all get permitted through the Village office, with inspections before the walls close. That sequence protects you, because somebody other than your contractor confirms the waterproofing and rough plumbing existed before tile hid them. We pull the permits, book the inspections and hand over closed-out paperwork the next buyer's inspector will ask for.

faqs.q: Is a zero-entry shower possible in a 1960s slab house?
faqs.a: Often, and it depends on what sits under the concrete. Recessing the pan means cutting the slab and sometimes rerouting a drain line, which is straightforward when the plumbing cooperates and costly when it does not. We scope that before you commit to the look. Where the slab genuinely refuses, a low-profile curb with a properly sloped pan delivers the same clean detail without a leak in year three.

faqs.q: The plumbing is original. Do we replace it during the bath?
faqs.a: If the walls and slab are open, replace it. Galvanized supply from this era is scaling shut and cast iron waste is at or beyond its service life, and new marble draining into a failing line is a poor trade. We run a camera through the drains early so the decision rests on footage rather than a hunch, and the work happens while access is free instead of after the stone is set.

faqs.q: Will a new bathroom window need Village approval?
faqs.a: If it changes the exterior, yes. Interior-only bath work goes through plan review and inspections without design review. Adding a window, enlarging one, or venting through a visible wall alters the elevation, so the citizen advisory board of Beach Club members comments on the design and the Village Council takes the action. Most bath scopes stay inside and skip that entirely. We identify which case is yours at the first walk-through.

faqs.q: Why do bathroom estimates vary so widely?
faqs.a: Because the visible half is easy to price and the hidden half is where honesty lives. Stone, glass and fittings set the tone, but slab cutting, drain relocation, waterproofing and replacing original pipe separate a real number from an attractive one. We scope the building rather than the mood board and give you a fixed written price. At this level the competition is on finish quality and certainty, not on being the lowest bidder.

bathroom-remodeling.cta_sub: Tell us what is wrong with it and we will come measure, scope and price the fix, in English o en español.

home-additions.title: Sea Ranch Lakes Home Additions, FL | PGX Builders
home-additions.meta_description: Additions in Sea Ranch Lakes, FL fit inside a 35-foot height limit and Village Council review. Engineered and fully permitted. (786) 273-2524.
home-additions.h1: Room to grow inside the gate
home-additions.hero_sub: Rear extensions, second stories and garage rebuilds in Sea Ranch Lakes, engineered, measured against the Village land development code, approved by the Council and built under the daily supervision of a licensed general contractor.
home-additions.local_heading: The rules that shape your addition
intro_paragraphs: Lots inside the Village are finite, resale is rare, and the people who own here tend to stay, which is why adding on is the usual answer to needing more house. The projects repeat: a rear extension toward Lake Seneca, a second story over a single-story block ranch on Saranac Road or Mendota Lane, a primary wing pushed back on an Intracoastal lot, a garage rebuilt with conditioned space above it. What almost never happens in Sea Ranch Lakes is a detached guest cottage, and the reason sits in the code rather than in anybody's taste.

This Village writes its dimensions down. Buildings stop at 35 feet above grade, measured to the highest structural component. The front setback is 25 feet; sides are 12 feet, 15 on the street side of a corner lot; the rear is 15 feet, and 25 feet where the lot fronts one of the interior lakes. At least 30 percent of the lot must stay pervious, every residence needs a garage of at least 450 square feet, and the residential district allows one single-family dwelling per lot and no accessory buildings. Plans travel from the Village Clerk to the building official to the Beach Club advisory board and then the Council.

Structural habits become visible the moment an addition goes up. New footings have to be tied to 1950s ones, tie beams and connections have to meet current standards, and the seam where old stucco meets new has to disappear or the whole thing reads as bolted on. We coordinate the engineering, sequence the work so the occupied half of the house stays livable, and keep the site tight because the lane out front belongs to your neighbors. Fixed written scope, daily supervision, one accountable team from feasibility through final inspection and warranty.
home-additions.scope_intro: Every addition starts with a survey, an engineer and a realistic read on setbacks, height and pervious area. These five come up most often.

scope_items.name: Extending toward Lake Seneca
scope_items.desc: Family rooms and primary suites pushed back within the 15-foot rear setback, or 25 feet on a lake lot, with foundations and roof tie-ins engineered together.

scope_items.name: Upstairs inside the height limit
scope_items.desc: Existing footings and walls evaluated first, then a full upper floor designed to stay under the Village's 35-foot height limit and satisfy the engineer.

scope_items.name: Garages rebuilt, not erased
scope_items.desc: Converting garage space only works if the required 450 square feet is rebuilt somewhere, so we plan that replacement into the drawings from the start.

scope_items.name: Attached suites for family
scope_items.desc: Guest and in-law suites built into the one permitted dwelling, with private bath and sitting room, because detached cottages are not allowed on these lots.

scope_items.name: Structure below the new rooms
scope_items.desc: Underpinning, new footings, column pads and tie-beam upgrades: the half of the budget nobody photographs and the half that decides whether it lasts.

faqs.q: How tall and how close to the line can I build?
faqs.a: The Village land development code states it plainly: 35 feet above grade measured to the highest structural component, a 25-foot front setback, 12-foot sides with 15 feet on the street side of a corner lot, and 15 feet at the rear, rising to 25 feet where your lot fronts Lake Cayuga or Lake Seneca. A minimum of 30 percent of the lot must stay pervious, which quietly caps the footprint before anyone argues about elevations.

faqs.q: Can I add a guest cottage for my parents?
faqs.a: Not as a separate building. The residential district permits one single-family dwelling per lot and allows no accessory buildings at all, so a detached cottage with its own kitchen is off the table here. What works is an attached wing with bedroom, bath, sitting area and a private entrance, built into the permitted house and designed so it reads as part of the original architecture. Most families who wanted a cottage prefer the wing once they see it drawn.

faqs.q: Does the flood zone limit what I can spend on the house?
faqs.a: It can. The Village adopts the FEMA flood maps and requires lowest-floor elevation certification in flood hazard areas. If the value of your improvements crosses the federal substantial-improvement threshold measured against the existing structure, the entire building has to be brought into flood compliance, not just the new portion. On a barrier island that arithmetic belongs at the front of design, not at permit intake. We run it early.

faqs.q: Can these old block houses actually carry a second floor?
faqs.a: Many can with reinforcement, some cannot, and a structural engineer settles it rather than an opinion at the curb. Original footings and block walls get evaluated, and where they fall short the remedy is new footings, columns or an upgraded tie beam designed into the project. Sometimes the honest recommendation is a rear extension instead, because it costs less and disturbs less. You get options with real numbers attached.

faqs.q: What should we expect from the approval process?
faqs.a: Plan in months rather than weeks. The application goes to the Village Clerk, is reviewed by the building official and the Village's consulting professionals, draws design comment from a citizen board of Beach Club members, and is acted on by the Council on its own meeting schedule. Tree removal carries a separate Village permit with replacement planting set by the Council, and work in the waterway brings Broward County in alongside the Village. None of it is fast, and all of it is knowable in advance.

home-additions.cta_heading: Let's see what the lot allows
home-additions.cta_sub: Bring the survey. We will walk setbacks, height, pervious area and honest numbers before you spend on drawings, in English o en español.

outdoor-living.title: Terraces & Pool Decks, Sea Ranch Lakes FL | PGX Builders
outdoor-living.meta_description: Outdoor living in Sea Ranch Lakes, FL — summer kitchens, covered terraces, pool decks and seawall coordination on lake and Intracoastal lots. (786) 273-2524.
outdoor-living.h1: Between the terrace and the seawall
outdoor-living.hero_sub: Summer kitchens, covered terraces, pergolas, driveways and seawall coordination for Sea Ranch Lakes homes, permitted through the Village, cleared with Broward County where water is involved, built by a licensed general contractor.
outdoor-living.local_heading: Outdoor rooms on a barrier island
intro_paragraphs: Nobody buys inside this gate for the interior. They buy for the lake at the back of the lot, the Intracoastal frontage, or the short walk across A1A to the Beach Club. So the yard is where the money goes: a covered terrace and summer kitchen behind a house on Cayuga Road, a pool deck and fire feature facing Lake Seneca, a rebuilt dock and lift on the waterway side. Underground utilities and mature canopy make these Sea Ranch Lakes yards look effortless, which is precisely why work in them has to be planned rather than improvised.

Exterior projects answer to more desks than interior ones. Structures, paving and utilities are permitted through the Village office. The code keeps pools and patios at least five feet off the rear lot line, holds any fence or hedge within 15 feet of the mean water line to three feet, requires 30 percent of the lot to remain pervious, and permits no accessory buildings at all. Docks and piers on the Intracoastal side require plans approved by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers; on the interior lakes, docks, piers and boathouses are not permitted. Broward County has its own say on seawall and marine work.

We build outdoors to indoor standards, because salt air audits everything. Gas, water and electrical for a summer kitchen get permitted and inspected instead of run under a paver. Pergola and trellis footings are engineered for High-Velocity Hurricane Zone wind loads. Metals are specified for coastal exposure, stone is sealed, and the terrace is pitched to send a South Florida downpour away from the house. Driveways meet the private street cleanly and drain to the swale. Fixed written scope, daily supervision, and a job site the neighbors never have to notice.
outdoor-living.scope_heading: What we build in the yard
outdoor-living.scope_intro: From a single terrace to a full rebuild between the house and the water, each piece gets designed, permitted and constructed as one job.

scope_items.name: Summer kitchens, salt-rated
scope_items.desc: Permitted services to a full cooking wall, marine-grade metals and sealed stone, specified for a lot taking salt air from two directions.

scope_items.name: Terraces and pergolas, anchored
scope_items.desc: Roofed outdoor rooms and shade structures on poured footings, with hardware rated for HVHZ wind loads, tied into the roofline instead of leaning on it.

scope_items.name: Pools, decks and setbacks
scope_items.desc: Pool and patio areas laid out to hold the required five feet off the rear lot line while staying inside the Village's 30 percent pervious minimum.

scope_items.name: Docks, lifts and seawalls
scope_items.desc: Dock, mooring and lift work on the Intracoastal side coordinated through Army Corps plan approval and the county review that seawall and marine work attracts.

scope_items.name: Driveways, stucco and paint
scope_items.desc: Paver and finished-concrete drives set level to the private street and draining to swale, plus stucco repair and exterior color the review board will see.

faqs.q: What approvals does a backyard project actually require?
faqs.a: More than a grill island suggests. Structures need a building permit, the gas, water and electrical runs need their own trade permits and inspections, and because all of it is visible from outside, the design draws comment from the Beach Club citizen board before the Village Council acts. Anything touching the waterway or a protected tree adds a further approval on top. We carry those approvals as part of the job instead of handing you a list and wishing you luck.

faqs.q: How does the seawall elevation rule affect an older wall?
faqs.a: The trigger is usually the repair itself. The Village code carries the regional standard: a new or substantially rehabilitated tidal flood barrier reaches a minimum of five feet NAVD88, with a transitional allowance for earlier applications where the wall is built to accept that height later. Patching a cap is one thing; rebuilding most of a wall pulls the whole run up to standard. Broward County has a say in the marine work, so elevation, design and schedule get settled before mobilization.

faqs.q: Can I put a shed out back for the pool equipment?
faqs.a: Not a freestanding one. The Village code does not allow accessory buildings at all, which surprises nearly everyone the first time they hear it. Equipment gets designed into the house, into an attached enclosure, or onto a screened and landscaped pad that respects the setbacks. It is a constraint worth respecting, since it is part of why these lanes look the way they do instead of like a row of resin boxes tucked behind hedges.

faqs.q: There is a mature tree where I want the terrace. Now what?
faqs.a: We design around it, or we apply, because the Village protects its canopy seriously. Removal requires a permit and replacement planting scaled to the canopy lost, taking off more than a quarter of a tree counts as hat racking and is prohibited, and every residential lot has to carry at least three trees, one category one and two category two, with a category one tree out front. Several species may not be planted at all. Shifting the footprint usually beats mitigation, and the finished yard looks better for it.

faqs.q: What does a full backyard project run?
faqs.a: Structure and utilities drive it far more than square footage does. A paver terrace with landscape lighting is one budget. A roofed outdoor room with a full summer kitchen, gas, water, power and a rebuilt pool deck is genuinely another, and dock or seawall work sits in its own category with county licensing attached. We walk the property, scope it in writing and price against a specification, so you compare real work instead of per-foot guesses.

outdoor-living.cta_heading: Bring us out to the yard
outdoor-living.cta_sub: Walk us from the terrace down to the water and tell us what you want. A written scope follows, in English o en español.

permitting-compliance.title: Sea Ranch Lakes Permit Records, FL | PGX Builders
permitting-compliance.meta_description: Open or expired permit on a Sea Ranch Lakes house? PGX files it, inspects it and closes it out at the Village office before your sale. (786) 273-2524.
permitting-compliance.h1: Decades of decisions, one open file
permitting-compliance.hero_sub: Permit applications, HVHZ product approvals, inspections and final sign-offs inside the Village of Sea Ranch Lakes, plus the open and expired permits a prior owner left behind. Licensed Florida general contractor, Lic. CGC1539072.
intro_paragraphs: Most permit trouble inside this gate is inherited. Turnover is rare, so when a Sea Ranch Lakes house finally changes hands the file carries decades of other people's decisions: jalousies swapped for impact glass by a company that closed, a Florida room glassed in on Saranac Road, a garage turned into an office, a dock and lift rebuilt after a storm, a service panel upgraded on a handshake. None of it shows in the house. All of it shows in a title search, an appraisal, or a lender's file three weeks before funding.

Permits here are filed at the Village office on Gatehouse Road, where the Village Clerk takes the application in, the building official and the Village's consulting professionals review it against the Florida Building Code and the Village land development code, the Beach Club citizen board comments on anything visible from outside, and the Council acts. Behind the Village sits the county: the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals publishes the amendments and certifies the officials and inspectors who will read your file. Broward is High-Velocity Hurricane Zone territory, so windows, doors and roofing need approved products with the anchor details attached.

PGX Builders Group has spent more than 20 years building in South Florida and delivered 150-plus remodels and additions, every one permitted and inspected, which is another way of saying we have read a great many bad files. We pull the address history before pricing anything, open up whatever has to be seen, and bring in the engineer, architect or surveyor the record requires instead of pretending to be one. Flood elevation gets checked early on the Intracoastal and lake lots, because crossing the substantial-improvement threshold changes the project. A supervisor books each inspection and meets the inspector at the gate. Nobody here is selling a shortcut.
permitting-compliance.scope_heading: Inside the gate, on the record
permitting-compliance.scope_intro: Some of this happens before a shovel moves. The rest happens because something already went sideways. Either way it starts with the record, not a phone call.

scope_items.name: Open files behind the gate
scope_items.desc: Requesting the full permit history for the address, establishing what was actually built, then reactivating, correcting or re-inspecting whatever the Village needs to close each one.

scope_items.name: Unpermitted work, documented
scope_items.desc: Enclosed Florida rooms, converted garages, added baths and windows swapped years ago, recorded as built, engineered where the code requires it, then inspected against today's standards.

scope_items.name: Approved products, proper anchors
scope_items.desc: Impact windows, doors and roofing with current High-Velocity Hurricane Zone approvals, installed to the anchor pattern the approval specifies and documented before the inspector asks.

scope_items.name: Inspections without a second trip
scope_items.desc: Trades staged so each phased inspection arrives genuinely ready, someone from PGX on site when the inspector clears the gatehouse, and the final actually called.

scope_items.name: Tree, dock and flood filings
scope_items.desc: Village tree removal and replacement planting, Army Corps and county approvals on the waterway side, and the elevation certification a flood-zone lot requires.

faqs.q: An open permit turned up on the house and the sale is moving. What now?
faqs.a: Start with the record. Ask the Village office for every permit ever pulled on the address, which inspections were signed off and where the file stopped. Then it becomes a diagnosis: sometimes only a final is missing, sometimes what was built no longer matches what was approved, and sometimes the permit sits under a contractor who went out of business years ago. All three have a path. None of them has a fast one, which is why the call should come now rather than the week of funding.

faqs.q: Which projects inside the Village actually need a permit?
faqs.a: More than owners expect. Anything touching structure, roofing, windows and doors, electrical, plumbing, gas or mechanical does, and so do pools, decks, driveways, docks, seawalls and fences. Taking down a tree carries its own Village permit with replacement planting set by the Council. Paint, flooring laid over an existing slab and cabinets replaced in place generally do not. The items that quietly go unfiled are the ones that cost most later: a garage converted, a porch glassed in, a panel changed, a water heater moved.

faqs.q: Is this a Village matter or a county matter?
faqs.a: Both, in different ways. The permit is issued through the Village office on Gatehouse Road, and the reviewing is done by the building official and the Village's consulting professionals, with the Beach Club citizen board commenting on exterior design and the Council taking final action. You do not file anything with Broward County, but its Board of Rules and Appeals certifies the people reviewing and inspecting and publishes the amendments they apply. A detail that cleared review in another county can still draw comments here.

faqs.q: Does milestone inspection or building recertification apply to my house?
faqs.a: Not to the houses. Florida's milestone inspection and structural integrity reserve study requirements reach condominium and cooperative buildings of three stories and up, and county recertification programs are aimed at multifamily and commercial buildings rather than single-family homes. The condominium that replaced the old Sea Ranch Hotel is a different conversation than a block ranch on Mendota Lane. Where a board already has an engineer's report in hand, PGX coordinates the licensed professional who signs it and builds the repair scope that follows.

faqs.q: What does it cost to put unpermitted work right?
faqs.a: It depends on what is behind the stucco, and anyone quoting before opening it is guessing. A missing final on sound work is a small item. A room built with no engineering, or a re-roof done without approved products, can mean exposing it and rebuilding to current code. Permit fees are set by the schedule and scale with the value of the work, so they are neither ours to discount nor to mark up. What you get is a written scope, real allowances and the bad news first.

permitting-compliance.cta_heading: Before the gate opens for a buyer
permitting-compliance.cta_sub: A permit number, a title report or just the address is enough to start. We come look, then tell you in writing what it takes, in English o en español.
